title: Trace-polynomial map between q- and p-degree Artin–Schreier covers
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, $q=p^r$ with $r\geq1$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ with prime subfield $\mathbf F_p$ and field trace $\operatorname{Tr}=\operatorname{Tr}_{k_0/\mathbf F_p}:k_0\to\mathbf F_p$ (as in [def-fd-additive-character]), and let $b\in k_0^\times$. Let $X$ be a separated $k_0$-scheme of finite type [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Put $\pi_q:Y_q=\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal O_X[y]/(y^q-y-f)\to X$ and $\pi_{p,b}:Y_{p,b}=\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal O_X[t]/(t^p-t-bf)\to X$, and let $\sigma_c$ ($c\in k_0$) be the $X$-automorphism of $Y_q$ given by $y\mapsto y+c$ and $\tau_d$ ($d\in\mathbf F_p$) the $X$-automorphism of $Y_{p,b}$ given by $t\mapsto t+d$. Then:

1. $\pi_q$ is finite étale, and on the geometric fibre of $Y_q$ over every geometric point of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] the group $(k_0,+)$ acts simply transitively through $c\mapsto\sigma_c$; in particular every geometric fibre has $q$ points.
2. The additive polynomial $\Theta_b(y)=\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}(by)^{p^i}$ satisfies $\Theta_b(y)^p-\Theta_b(y)=b(y^q-y)$ in $\mathcal O_X[y]$, hence $\Theta_b(y)^p-\Theta_b(y)=bf$ in $\mathcal O_X[y]/(y^q-y-f)$, so $t\mapsto\Theta_b(y)$ defines an $X$-morphism $\theta_b:Y_q\to Y_{p,b}$.
3. $\theta_b\circ\sigma_c=\tau_{\operatorname{Tr}(bc)}\circ\theta_b$ for every $c\in k_0$.
4. On the geometric fibres over every geometric point of $X$, $\theta_b$ is surjective, and each of its fibres is an orbit, under the $\sigma_c$, of the subgroup $\ker(c\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}(bc))$ of order $q/p$.
5. For every morphism $h:X'\to X$ of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, with $f'=h^*f$ and $Y'_q$, $Y'_{p,b}$, $\sigma'_c$, $\tau'_d$, $\theta'_b$ formed from $(X',f')$ in the same way, the canonical isomorphisms $Y'_q\cong Y_q\times_XX'$ and $Y'_{p,b}\cong Y_{p,b}\times_XX'$ carry $\sigma'_c$, $\tau'_d$ and $\theta'_b$ to the base changes of $\sigma_c$, $\tau_d$ and $\theta_b$.
